About.title: About NatureLog
About.subtitle: The free nature journal for wildlife observations in Germany.
About.whatText: NatureLog is a free web app for recording your wildlife sightings. The lexicon covers {count} species native to Germany – birds, mammals, amphibians, reptiles and a selection of insects, spiders and other invertebrates – with profile, size, habitat and conservation status. Mark every species you spot in the wild as seen and add your best photo of it. Step by step, that becomes your personal nature journal.

audience.birders: Birdwatchers who keep a species list
audience.photographers: Nature photographers who want their best wildlife photos in one place
audience.families: Families and children exploring the nature on their doorstep
audience.schools: Teachers and school classes learning about native species
audience.walkers: Anyone who wants to know which animal they just saw on a walk

About.freeText: NatureLog is a free project from Germany. Registration and every feature are free of charge. Use NatureLog right in your browser or install it on your phone as an app – no app store needed.

Faq.title: Frequently asked questions
Faq.subtitle: Everything important about NatureLog at a glance.

whatIs.a: NatureLog is a free nature journal in your browser. Record which animals you have seen in the wild, add your best photo of each species and share your sightings with other nature lovers.

free.a: Yes. Registration and every feature are free, and there is no subscription. NatureLog is a free project – if you like, you can support it with a donation.

app.q: Is there a NatureLog app for Android and iPhone?
app.a: NatureLog is a web app you can install without an app store. On Android, open naturelog.de in Chrome and choose “Install app” or “Add to home screen”. On iPhone, open the site in Safari, tap “Share” and then “Add to Home Screen”.

species.q: Which animals are in the lexicon?
species.a: The lexicon contains {count} species native to Germany: birds, mammals, amphibians, reptiles and a selection of insects, spiders and other invertebrates. Each species has a profile with size, habitat, conservation status, when to see it and similar species.

identify.q: Can NatureLog help me identify an animal?
identify.a: Yes, in two ways. In the lexicon you narrow species down with filters for animal group, order, colour, size and conservation status. You can also upload a photo and search it with Google Lens.

record.q: How do I record a sighting?
record.a: Create a free account, open the species in the lexicon and mark it as seen. It then appears in your collection, where you can add your own photo.

photos.q: Can I upload and share my own wildlife photos?
photos.a: Yes. You can upload your favourite photo for every species you have seen. If your profile is public, your photos also appear on that species' lexicon page. Uploaded photos are checked against our content rules.

privacy.a: You decide: set your profile to public or private in the settings. A private profile is visible only to people you follow who also follow you. You can also keep species lists private, for example for your target species.

missing.q: What if a species is missing from the lexicon?
missing.a: Use “Suggest a missing animal” in the lexicon to propose new species. You can also submit improvements to existing texts right on a species' page.

deleteAccount.a: Yes, at any time in the settings. This also deletes your sightings and photos. Details on how your data is handled are in the privacy policy.

Faq.contact: Get in touch through the contact form.
